newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Storebrand has lower Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Storebrand has lower Q1 profits.

text.p: Storebrand ASA, Norway's biggest insurer, said on Tuesday lower financial income in non-life insurance helped slash first-quarter book profits by more than 40 percent to 141 million crowns ($19.9 million).
The result fell below market expectations and the share was down 0.70 percent to 43.20 crowns in early afternoon trade on the Oslo Bourse.
Storebrand is expected to merge at the end of this year with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, forming the biggest financial institution in the country.
Storebrand's group operating profit came to 1.13 billion crowns, which is 249 million crowns lower than in the corresponding 1996 period.
After distributing profits to life and pension policyholders, the group's book profit fell to 141 million crowns from 246 million.

"The main reason is lower financial income in non-life insurance," a statement said. "The result is also influenced by the good financial income in life assurance, continued sharp competition in non-life insurance, and a positive development in operating costs. The group's solidity continues to be very satisfactory."
At the end of the first quarter, Storebrand non-life had an operating profit of 24 million crowns, compared to 109 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Storebrand Livforsikring had an operating profit of 1.14 billion crowns against 1.30 billion for the same period last year.
The statement said 985 million crowns were allocated to policyholders, leaving 154 million to equity and tax.
Premium income for own account from life assurance rose by more than 24 percent to 2.93 billion crowns.
"High realised net gains on equities and interest-bearing instruments is the main reason for the life company continuing to record high financial income," the statement said.

Together with low operating costs, the high financial income was the main reason for the good operating result from life assurance. Net gains on securities in the life assurance company amounted to 682 million crowns in the first quarter, compared with 734 million in the corresponding period last year.

Unrealised gains rose by 562 million to stand at 5.14 billion crowns, including 3.80 billion in unrealised gains on equities. Investments in shares rose to almost 20 percent of the total investment portfolio.
Investments in the international stock markets rose to 44 percent of the share portfolio at the end of the first quarter, up from 36 percent at the start of the year.
